checks.detail: toned.md conforms to the CSA Template structure: Executive Summary; Current Microsoft Cloud Security Posture with Posture Summary, Key Risk Themes, Domain Posture, and Control Movement and Baseline Changes; Security Signal Review with Identity and Access, Endpoint and Vulnerabilities, Data Protection and Collaboration, Cloud Workload and Attack Path Exposure, AI Agents and Generative AI Usage, and Detection and Operational Readiness; Recommended Security Actions with Security Awareness, Active Recommendations, CIS Microsoft 365 Foundation Benchmark, Deferred Recommendations, and Recommendation History. Each substantive domain leads with a supported conclusion (condition, quarter movement, evidence, significance, qualification, recommended response) and interprets Microsoft/CIS/NIST inputs as supporting evidence rather than narrative voice. Quarterly thesis is established with preceding-vs-current-quarter comparisons for identity (48.33% vs 44.42% and 43.85%; MFA 2.14/9 vs 1.99/9; legacy blocking 7.93/8 regression), Data (0%), and Apps (35.86%), with explicit statements where comparison is unsupported (endpoint, AI, audit). Cross-signal synthesis groups related controls into themes (authentication/privileged access, impersonation, information protection, external collaboration, logging/detection). No Microsoft-style noun stacks or product-vendor grammar observed; positive findings carry limitations and gaps are scoped as known/unknown. Security Awareness section is exempted from the conclusion-first requirement but still satisfies substance freeze and banned-pattern checks.

Every numeric token, date, percentage, measurement, control-point value, CIS reference, NIST reference, classification outcome, and recommendation in toned.md was traced back to draft.md unchanged. Verified samples: 37.49%/36.72%/36.61%; 48.33%/44.42%/43.85%; 100.48/268; 46.08%; 55.54%; 2.14/9; 9.41/10; 7.93/8; 1.99/9; 1.85/9; 2.06/9; 0.15; 0.07; 8/8; 0/8; 0/5; 0/2; 0/3; 0/5; 1/1; 0/5; 0/5; 4/4; 1/1; 0/8; 0/7; 3/3; 0/1; 101/131; 103/130; CIS 5.2.2.1/5.2.2.2/5.2.2.3; 1.3.1; 7.2.1; 3.2.1; 3.3.1; 3.1.1; 6.1.2; 6.2.1; 2.1.1/2.1.4/2.1.5/2.1.7; 5.1.5.1; 6.5.1; NIST PR.AA-03, PR.AA-05, PR.PS-01, PR.PS-04, PR.DS-01, PR.DS-02, PR.DS-10, PR.AT-01, PR.AT-02, DE.CM-09; recommendation IDs 0-5 and their identification quarters. The Q2026 3 typo in the Active Recommendations row 4 status cell was corrected to 2026 Q3 with no factual change. No table row or cell meaning shifted; no narrative framing introduced a fact, cause, or outcome absent from draft.md.

Independent semantic inventory of draft.md entities, measurements, findings, and recommendations confirms one-to-one presence in toned.md with identical client-facing meaning. Verified: all five Priority 0-5 recommendations retain their strength (Confirm identity security model; Complete MFA coverage; Strengthen impersonation and collaboration protection; Establish sensitive-data controls; Validate audit coverage; Tighten information and meeting access). No recommendation was upgraded or downgraded. Findings on the uncredited intelligence-based impersonation protection (0/8), uncredited collaboration Safe Attachments (0/5), uncredited Office Safe Links (0/3), uncredited DLP (0/5), uncredited published labels (0/2), uncredited audit controls (0/3 each), and the Security Defaults/Conditional Access decision (originating 2023 Q3) are preserved with the same scope and attribution. Historical MFA registration counts (101/131 and 103/130) remain explicitly framed as historical-only with no Q3 account-level registration report. Measurement movement is attributed to population change where Microsoft reports it, not to verified remediation. No cause/effect claim was re-attributed and no metric was restated on a different basis.
